correctness.rationale: The domain is ALL binary overlap-free linear words of length 0..96 having exactly nine nonempty square factors. Every root has length <=40 because eight other squares require at least 16 positions; the block generator therefore exhausts 154 eligible square blocks. The inductive nine-level search retains all overlap-free products and ordered recipes, while independent full-prefix search tests all overlap-free words to length 96 and all square-suffix decompositions. The two finite approaches give counts {48:2,76:2,86:4,92:2,96:2}, zero at all other lengths <=96, and one nine-block recipe per word. No claim for n>96.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Shallit proves 10 concatenated squares force an overlap, and gives nine-square witness; the published sharp minimum-spectrum for k<=9 gives the minimum at k=9 (48) and its two minimizers. Neither enumerates every nine-square overlap-free product of lengths 49..96.
searches: overlap-free binary words concatenations of nine squares length spectrum 48 to 96 uniqueness Shallit

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The minimum-length result implies the two 48-letter cases with unique decompositions. The 10-square exclusion is used only to bound dynamic-program counts. Neither entails 76/86/92/96 counts or nonattainable intermediate lengths; obtaining those needs the complete length-bounded census.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Complementing bits identifies paired words but does not imply the five nonzero length fibers. Thue-Morse doubling maps the 48-word witness to 96 but gives no exclusion of other lengths or uniqueness. General ten-square impossibility and minimum-length results imply only the initial boundary, not the full window.
